t: The organist and choirmaster and the civilian instructors in the departments of foreign languages and tactics at the United States Military Academy who are serving under appointments made prior to January 17, 1963, are entitled to public quarters without charge, and to fuel and light without charge when they occupy public quarters.

fable.w: This section only grants a housing and utilities entitlement to certain civilian staff at the United States Military Academy. The tempting reading is that the mention of "civilian" instructors and "public" quarters signals outside-party involvement, but these are federal employees receiving a benefit, and "public quarters" simply means government housing. No one outside the federal government is consulted, heard, or given a right to sue over any federal decision.
fable.s: are entitled to public quarters without charge, and to fuel and light without charge when they occupy public quarters
